messages:
Ria (support): AcmeOps reporting sharp p95/p99 regression on /v1/generate since ~09:12 UTC. Their dashboard shows median ~1.8s but p95 jumped to ~6s and p99 to ~18s. They also see a spike in 'queued' and occasional 429s. Customer is on hosted, region eu-west-1, model redwood-large-qa.
Sam (eng-runtime): thx Ria — any request ids or short sample? can you paste the top traces?
Ria (support): pasted a short stack from their trace: 
```
REQUEST_ID=req_8f3a
route=/v1/generate
worker=worker-gpu-3
queue_wait_ms=11500
processing_ms=320
status=200
```
They sent curl repro: 
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"redwood-large-qa","input":"summarize...","max_tokens":256}'
```
AcmeOps says load is similar to normal (not a big spike).
Luca (eng-sre): early guess: worker-gpu-3 shows CPU pinned + cgroups throttling under sustained kv-cache growth? could be a live GC or memory pressure causing longer scheduling. I'll check host metrics.
infra-bot: host/worker-gpu-3 metrics pushed: cpu_util=98%, load=11.2, net_rx=120MB/s, gpu_mem_free=2.1GB, process_rss=48GB, oom_events=0 in last 6h.
Sam (eng-runtime): interesting — if KV cache growth is pushing eviction and causing long pauses on the inference process we can see queue pileup upstream. Any recent model variant/quant change deployed?
Elena (eng-platform): we rolled a small kernel patch to the synchronous scheduler at 02:30 UTC yesterday for sequence-prefetch optimization — but rollout to eu-west-1 was gradual and finished 06:15 UTC. Not many errors flagged during canary.
Ria (support): customer says regression started after 09:00 UTC in their logs.
Luca (eng-sre): I'm seeing correlated queue depth on the admission controller for tenant acme-inc: concurrent_open_requests peaked and stay higher. Admission latencies spiked from ~12ms -> 1.2s during the window.
Sam (eng-runtime): can we get a per-request trace for one p99? need the admission time, scheduling time, and decode time. Ria can you request one or get a sample from customer?
Ria (support): got one sample request id req_9a7b, attached full trace from our app logs.
Sam (eng-runtime): pasted trace looks like: 
```
admission_check=320ms
enqueue_wait=11200ms
assigned_worker=worker-gpu-3
start_processing=11520ms
kv_cache_load=850ms
decode=210ms
```
That enqueue_wait indicates real queueing upstream. root cause likely worker processing slowness (kv_cache_load + prefetch).
Luca (eng-sre): immediate mitigation: 1) route AcmeOps traffic to eu-central-1 fallback pool (compatible model) 2) bump concurrency limit for tenant temporarily and increase pool size if autoscaler can. I'm running scale action now.
Elena (eng-platform): autoscaler triggered +2 replicas in the eu-west-1 GPU small pool but workers are slow to warm due to model weights load (cold start ~45s) so routing is quicker. Triggering route-move for this tenant to fallback pool (eu-central-1) with smaller model redwood-medium-qa and enabling structured output toggle. @Ria pls confirm we can do fallback.
Ria (support): confirmed with customer — they prefer degraded perf over p99 spikes; they accept fallback to redwood-medium-qa for next 90m.
infra-bot: route-move job started: job_id=rm_7732 -> moving tenant acme-inc -> eu-central-1:fallback-pool.
Sam (eng-runtime): parallel triage: I'm going to repro locally with a synthetic stream that forces KV cache churn. steps: 1) run 200 concurrent requests with same prompt pattern 2) inspect process thread stacks 3) enable debug logs for cache hits.
Sam (eng-runtime): repro produced similar enqueue_wait when kv_cache hit ratio drops below 0.6. Observed goroutine/stall in scheduler while compacting the KV index with approx 700ms pauses every few requests.
Luca (eng-sre): ok that matches. longer-term: we need to add backpressure on KV cache compaction or move compaction off hot path. Short-term patch: reduce per-worker max_cache_size via dynamic config and restart one worker at a time to apply. @Elena can you push config change for eu-west-1 pool?
Elena (eng-platform): pushing dynamic config now: `workers.pool.eu-west-1.max_kv_cache_bytes=12_000_000_000` (was 24_000_000_000). Rolling restart set to drain and restart one-by-one. This should reduce compaction frequency.
Ria (support): applied, customer confirm p95 dropped from 6s -> 1.9s in fallback pool, p99 down to ~4.2s. They still see occasional 429s while the route-move completes.
Customer-Acct-Rep: customer appreciated quick fallback, flagged they'd like postmortem and SLA credit review. Passing to CS.
Sam (eng-runtime): follow ups for postmortem: 1) reproduce compaction stall with unit test and add perf guard 2) make KV compaction async or incremental 3) add admission-side early signal so we can reject or reroute before queue piles if worker signals compaction_lock.
Luca (eng-sre): also add better alert: p95/p99 divergence with queue depth delta > 500 and admission latency > 500ms -> auto route to fallback pool.
Elena (eng-platform): I'll draft the configuration change and revert plan. Also scheduling a canary for the scheduler patch.
Ria (support): closing loop for customer: we told AcmeOps we've moved them to fallback pool and will follow up with a postmortem and credit if applicable. They asked for repro steps so engineering recorded them.
Sam (eng-runtime): repro steps (short): 
1) Run 150-250 concurrent requests against redwood-large-qa with repeating prompt patterns to force KV cache thrash.
2) Observe worker metrics: `cache_hits_ratio`, `compaction_lock_time_ms`.
3) Collect trace where `enqueue_wait > 5s`.
Commands: 
```
ab -n 2000 -c 200 -T 'application/json' -p payload.json https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
# or use our perf-hammer: ./perf-hammer --concurrency 200 --rate 40 --model redwood-large-qa --pattern repeat
```
Expected signals: cache_hits_ratio < 0.7, compaction_lock_time spikes, admission_queue_depth increases.
Elena (eng-platform): ticket created: PLAT-9876 with config changes and rollback. Runtime ticket RT-4321 for async compaction work. SRE ticket SRE-210 for alert.
Luca (eng-sre): monitoring: set temporary Grafana alert threshold and created runbook steps: 1) route to fallback 2) bump pool size 3) roll config change 4) one-by-one worker restart.
Ria (support): customer happy for now. I'll send the summary and link to PLAT-9876. Thanks all. :tada:
Sam (eng-runtime): posting note: once compaction fix lands we should gradually restore original max_kv_cache_bytes after validating compaction no longer pauses scheduler.
Ria (support): thread resolved. I'll follow up with CS on credit request and paste postmortem when ready.
